A1.justification: Both complete 17-page PDFs describe the same F2R research, with readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original F2R benchmark results on DAVIS, Set8 and CRVD, together with component, stage and temporal-window ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and ablation results, with revised CRVD values and a replaced qualitative example.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same blind estimator, spatial refiner, residual inputs, FAAM/FDAM components, training objectives and inference procedure. Diagram typography changes do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use DAVIS 2017, Set8 and CRVD indoor for the same synthetic Gaussian and real raw video-denoising tasks. Figure 4 substitutes an illustrative DAVIS example without expanding the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2 and 7 and the qualitative comparisons. The revised Figure 4 retains NAFNet, FastDVDNet, FloRNN, UDVD and TAP.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains identical splits, noise settings, preprocessing, metrics and training settings, including 256 x 256 crops, batch size 4, 200K iterations and temporal windows of 9 and 7. The existing ablation protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 and Section 4.2 replace the tractor text-edge case study with a car-race dashboard example discussing detail recovery despite motion blur. The stage, component, alignment-module and temporal-window ablation designs remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new Table 3 rounding explanation concerns displayed precision rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises F2R's CRVD PSNR downward at four ISO levels: the average changes from 45.71 to 45.69 dB and ISO 25600 from 42.86 to 42.82 dB, also updated in Table 3. The stated advantage over TAP changes from 0.56 to 0.54 dB. Figure 4 replaces tractor results with car-race results; these are different examples, not a same-setting performance change. Synthetic aggregate results and rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, noise-independence assumptions and Equations 1–4 are unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about spatiotemporal decoupling, residual-domain learning and superior self-supervised denoising performance. The numerical revisions do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the tractor text-boundary interpretation with an explanation that complementary temporal cues recover dashboard markings even when the clean reference is motion-blurred. Table 3 additionally attributes identical baseline and Stage 2-only displayed scores to rounding.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's actual contents or usability.

R1.justification: The same 43 references and research-positioning arguments are retained. Bibliographic edits standardize venue names and formatting without adding or removing cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized revisions to the qualitative-results discussion and captions, adds acknowledgements and author identifiers, and standardizes bibliography formatting. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 replaces its upper example and adjusts panel arrangement. Figures 2–3 receive typography adjustments, Figures 4–5 lose yellow-arrow annotations, and Table 3 gains a caption clarification. Table 2 moves from page 12 to page 11, with associated layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The added code-access information and Table 3 rounding explanation modestly improve reproducibility documentation and reporting clarity. The small CRVD score revisions preserve the reported rankings, while the method and experimental scope remain stable. These are limited documentation benefits; the PDFs do not establish external code usability or substantial empirical strengthening.
